facts.text: PlasticineEnv subclasses gym.Env, takes cfg_path, version and nn, builds a Taichi environment and initializes it

The environment id is built at import as f'{env_name}-v{id+1}' for ten names and variants 1 to 5, registered with entry_point plb.envs.env:PlasticineEnv, kwargs cfg_path and version, and max_episode_steps 50
The README's usage example runs Move-v1
The action space is Box(-1, 1, (action_dim,)) and the observation space is Box(-inf, inf, obs.shape)
__init__ captures the initial state with taichi_env.get_state() and then calls reset()
reset() takes no seed or options, restores the initial state captured at construction, clears the recorded actions and returns _get_obs()
_get_obs concatenates every step_size-th particle's position and velocity with the state of every primitive
step() advances the Taichi environment, computes the loss, appends the action, and returns (observation, reward, False, loss_info); the done flag is always False
The observation stride is len(x) // n_observed_particles
Move has two Sphere primitives and each declares a 3-dimensional action with scale (0.01, 0.01, 0.01)
Primitives.action_dim is the sum of the action dims of its primitives
Primitives.set_action flattens the action and clips every element to the interval [-1, 1]
A primitive state is a 3-value position plus a 4-value rotation quaternion, returned by get_state
The default number of observed particles is 200
Move sets the particle count to 10000
SIMULATOR.quality defaults to 1
SIMULATOR.dt is 0.5e-4 / quality seconds and SIMULATOR.substeps is int(2e-3 / dt), so at the default quality 1 one environment step is 40 physics substeps of 0.05 ms (2 ms)
MPMSimulator.step advances the simulation from the current frame by substeps frames
The reward is the start loss minus the step's incremental loss, returned inside loss_info
Taichi is initialized on the GPU at import

determinism.notes: PlasticineEnv.reset() takes no seed: it restores the state captured at construction, so a fresh reset plus the same action sequence repeats on one backend. cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 accept and echo a seed, but it labels the episode and does not change the initial state. The upstream initializes Taichi on the GPU and its MPM scatter accumulates floating-point contributions in parallel, so bit-identical replay across devices is not claimed; the package claims seeded (labelled) replay, not exact.

gaps: the deployed model is an MPM soft-body continuum with gravity, contacts, friction and yield stress (F1: physics with contacts), but it models no actuator, sensor or noise dynamics, so F2 is not claimed

the fake backend is a pure-Python stand-in for the interface, not the solver: it holds 200 observed particle positions and velocities as fixed placeholder data and moves only the two primitive kinematic states by action * 0.01 per step; it models no soft-body deformation, contact, friction, gravity, yield stress or rendering

the real Move-v1 observation has 1214 values (200 observed particles x 6 position/velocity values plus 2 primitives x 7 state values); the fake returns the same 1214-value length but its particle values are placeholders and its reward is always 0.0 with an empty info object, so the loss and inverse-IoU measurements are not modelled
the fake implements the registration's 50-step episode limit as truncated=True; PlasticineEnv.step itself always returns done=False and the legacy gym TimeLimit wrapper is what ends the episode
the physics substep is 0.5e-4 s (0.05 ms) and one environment step is 40 substeps (2 ms); timestep_ms names the 2 ms environment step that one cap.world.step.v1 tick advances
the fake ignores the reset seed and the reset options, matching the upstream reset() signature; the seed only labels the episode
the sim backend (gymnasium.make('Move-v1') through the legacy gym registration, with Taichi on the GPU) was not run: the gate does not install or import the clone
snapshot and restore are not offered: PlasticineEnv exposes no get_state/set_state of its own (the state lives on its taichi_env attribute)
no rendering is bound: cap.world.render.v1 needs an artifact store that OpenMHS 0.9 does not have
no physical device is modelled and the benchmark was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop the runtime refuses step and reset until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the last world state stays readable
